learningObjective: Distinguish Relax graph-level fusion from TensorIR loop-level fusion.

canonicalClaims.claim: TVM performs fusion at two levels: (1) Relax graph-level fusion groups ops into a fused sub-function to reduce kernel launches; (2) TensorIR loop-level fusion via `compute_inline`/`compute_at` merges producer/consumer loops within a PrimFunc to eliminate intermediates and improve locality.
conditions: Both levels honor fusion policies and dependence constraints.
nonImplications: Does not imply fusion always improves performance.
Does not imply the two levels are redundant; they compose.

misconceptions.claim: Relax fuses arbitrary op pairs with no fusion boundary.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Relax uses per-op patterns and policies; fusion boundaries exist.

misconceptions.claim: External calls (cuBLAS/cuDNN) can be loop-fused with generated PrimFuncs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Extern calls are opaque; only epilogue-style graph-level linking is possible in limited cases.

misconceptions.claim: Graph-level and loop-level fusion are the same optimization at different names.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They operate on different IRs and at different scales.

misconceptions.claim: Fusion is always a monotonic win.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Over-fusion can spike register/SMEM pressure and hurt occupancy.

implementationFacts: Relax fusion transforms produce fused sub-functions calling a merged PrimFunc.
